evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:103-108, 123-131, 172-177, 191-201 — all four write mutation handlers (handlePetDelete, handlePetReview, handleVehicleDelete, handleVehicleReview) wrap mutateAsync in try/catch whose catch body is ONLY `console.error(...)`. On a failed delete or approve/review the confirm dialog closes, nothing is shown to the user, and the list re-renders unchanged — so a failed destructive/approval action is indistinguishable from success to the manager performing it.

This is the exact regression the sibling page was already fixed and test-guarded against: RegistryRulesPage.tsx:47-57 keeps the console.error for diagnostics but ALSO calls showToast({type:'error', ...}) 'so a failed save can never look like a success', and RegistryRulesPage.test.tsx:1-6 documents that the pre-fix handler 'only called console.error — no user-visible side effect'. RegistryPage.tsx never got the same treatment: it imports neither useToast nor any error-surface (grep of the file shows no useToast/showToast/setError), and the underlying hooks carry no central onError either — frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/hooks/useRegistry.ts has zero onError/useToast/toast references, confirming the error is swallowed end-to-end.

Impact: silent data-mutation failure on a user-facing manager workflow (pet/vehicle registration delete + approve). Landable frontend-only fix: inject useToast() into RegistryPage and replace each `console.error(...)`-only catch with an error toast (mirroring RegistryRulesPage.handleSubmit), preferably surfacing err.message when err instanceof Error; add a RegistryPage.test.tsx asserting the toast fires on mutateAsync rejection, same shape as the existing RegistryRulesPage test. Reachability traced from the rendered PetRegistrationList/VehicleRegistrationList onDelete/onReview props back to these handlers; kept at medium because confirming the invisible-failure UX requires a runtime mutation rejection, which static analysis cannot execute.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:87, 91, 137, 156, 160, 206 — all six intra-app navigations (view/edit/create for pets and vehicles) are done with `window.location.href = '/registry/...'`, triggering a full browser document reload inside what is a react-router SPA. Every other registry/marketplace page in the churn set uses react-router (RegistryRulesPage.tsx:9,62 uses useNavigate(); the page is reached via a routed <Route>).

Consequence: each 'View'/'Edit'/'Add' click tears down and re-bootstraps the whole React app — auth context re-init, TanStack Query cache discarded, i18n re-load, and a visible white flash — instead of a client-side route transition. It also makes the navigation untestable with the MemoryRouter used elsewhere and defeats SPA prefetch/state preservation. This is a correctness/UX smell, not just style, because it silently drops in-memory app state (e.g. unsaved filters on sibling screens) on every registry navigation.

Landable frontend-only fix: replace the window.location.href assignments with a useNavigate() navigate('/registry/...') (RegistryPage already renders inside the router), matching the canonical pattern already used in RegistryRulesPage.tsx. Low severity (+1): no data loss within this page, but it degrades the SPA contract on a high-churn manager screen. Medium confidence: the full-reload behaviour of window.location.href assignment is certain; the user-visible blast radius depends on surrounding app state that static analysis cannot enumerate.
